solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique after crossings); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Pet — roughly speaking, a fool

parts.note: roughly is circa, abbreviated CA
a noodle is a silly person

explanation.surface: Someone calls their pet, loosely speaking, a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: Pet looks like a noun for an animal, but here it is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To canoodle is to kiss and cuddle amorously, which is what petting means as a verb.

clue.text: Keep check, receiving a word of thanks

indicators.note: something receiving a thing takes it inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: to rein in is to check or restrain
ta is informal British for thank you

explanation.surface: A cheque is held back while someone waits for thanks.
explanation.walkthrough: Check looks like a noun, a cheque or bill, but it is the verb meaning restrain.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to continue possessing it rather than giving it up, a plain synonym.

clue.text: See papa getting bothered over daughter being placated

indicators.note: in a down entry, one piece sitting over another comes before it in the grid
something bothered is disturbed and stirred up, so the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A girl's dad gets worked up over her until he is calmed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone appeased has been pacified by having their demands met, the same as being soothed into calm.

clue.text: Past glories initially making one very keen

parts.note: ago means in the past

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the first letter of glories

explanation.surface: Memories of former triumphs leave someone thrilled and eager.
explanation.definitionFit: Agog describes eager excitement and anticipation, someone waiting impatiently with great interest.

clue.text: Some comedians were giving a reply

indicators.note: some of the words means only part of their run of letters is wanted

parts.note: found inside letters 7-12 of 'comedians were'

explanation.surface: A few comics were offering a comeback.
explanation.definitionFit: An answer is a response given to a question, a direct synonym of the noun meaning reply.

clue.text: Worker, one not pro

parts.note: a worker ant, the usual crossword worker
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An employee declares themselves against something.
explanation.definitionFit: Anti means opposed or against, the opposite stance from someone in favour of something.

clue.text: Drink after very final message

indicators.note: after places the first named piece behind the second in the answer

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very
ale is a drink, beer

explanation.surface: A last pint after a very final goodbye note.
explanation.walkthrough: Vale is Latin for farewell, used in English for a parting word.
explanation.definitionFit: Vale is a Latin farewell, a goodbye said at a parting or at a death.

clue.text: Composer non-believer? In one!

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen, outside the main religions
taken as written
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Was the composer an unbeliever? Yes, the exclamation says, one of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the celebrated Italian violin virtuoso who also wrote music, notably the Caprices.

clue.text: House by river with virtuoso poet

parts.note: HO is the abbreviation for house
R is the abbreviation for river
an ace is an expert, a star performer

explanation.surface: A riverside house shared with a brilliant poet.
explanation.definitionFit: Horace was the great Roman lyric poet of the Augustan age, author of the Odes.

clue.text: A cart led by good knight

indicators.note: being led by something means it comes first, in front

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good
A plus wain, an old word for a farm wagon

explanation.surface: A cart pulled along behind a noble knight.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Gawain is one of King Arthur's Round Table knights, hero of the Green Knight poem.

clue.text: A base for thieves maybe in port

parts.note: taken as written
a den of thieves is their hideout; maybe marks it as one example of a den

explanation.surface: A harbour serves as a hideout for robbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Aden is a seaport city in Yemen at the mouth of the Red Sea, once a British coaling station.

clue.text: A rise lad negotiated to be regularly paid

indicators.note: things negotiated are worked over and rearranged into a new deal

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: A young man bargains for a pay increase so he gets a steady wage.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaried worker receives a fixed annual sum in monthly instalments rather than hourly wages.

clue.text: US city gave lass shivers

indicators.note: shivers suggests shaking or shattering into pieces, so the letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: An American city sent a cold thrill through a girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Las Vegas is the Nevada desert city famous for its casinos and entertainment strip.

clue.text: Request measure leading to agreement

indicators.note: one piece leading to another stands in front of it

parts.note: an en is a printer's unit of width
a treaty is a formal pact

explanation.surface: An appeal is a step on the way to a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An entreaty is an earnest plea or appeal, asking for something with feeling.

clue.text: Islands where male meets females at matches

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
the women at weddings, which are matches in the marital sense

explanation.surface: An island spot where men meet women at sporting fixtures.
explanation.walkthrough: Matches suggests games, but here it means marriages.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hebrides are the archipelago off Scotland's west coast, split into Inner and Outer groups.

clue.text: President has soldiers once more out of India

parts.note: the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

indicators.note: with a letter taken out of the phrase before it, that letter is dropped

parts.note: again means once more
I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A president sends troops back in, this time withdrawing from India.
explanation.walkthrough: I is taken from AGAIN, leaving RE + AGAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth holder of the top office in the United States, serving through the 1980s.

clue.text: Eg, London society — not so English

indicators.note: not tells you the following words are to be left out of the longer word

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: London's high society is described as less English than it was.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove SO and E from SOCIETY, leaving CITY.
explanation.definitionFit: London is an example of a large important town, so Eg marks the definition by example.

clue.text: Something shiny in church, see

parts.note: CH is the abbreviation for church
the Holy See, the Pope's seat, is in Rome

explanation.surface: Look at the gleaming object inside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: A see is a bishop's seat; Rome is the Holy See.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrome is the bright metallic plating on car trim and taps, prized for its polished gleam.

clue.text: Run in country producing injury

indicators.note: in places the first piece inside the second

parts.note: a European nation
R is the cricket abbreviation for a run

explanation.surface: A jog abroad leaves a runner hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: R for run is a cricket scoring abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprain is damage to a ligament from a sudden twist, typically of an ankle or wrist.

clue.text: Long wood

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to yearn for something
second meaning: timber from a conifer tree

explanation.walkthrough: Long wood reads as a plank's length; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for yearning wistfully and a noun for timber cut from evergreen conifers.

clue.text: Christmas story book lacking central element

indicators.note: lacking its central element means the middle letter is dropped

parts.note: a novel is a book telling a story

explanation.surface: A festive storybook is missing an important part.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter V goes from NOVEL, leaving NOEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Noel is a name for the festive season, from the French word for the Yuletide holiday.

clue.text: Learner not the first person to be paid for work

definitions.text: person to be paid for work

indicators.note: not the first means the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A trainee is not the first in line for wages.
explanation.definitionFit: An earner is someone who receives income in return for labour, a wage-earner.

clue.text: One way of saying artist entered secretly

indicators.note: the setter asks for a different phrasing of the words that follow, here with their order inverted

parts.note: entered means came in, phrased the inverted way as in came
RA is a Royal Academician, the usual crossword artist

explanation.surface: A story of a painter slipping in unseen.
explanation.walkthrough: The artist entered can be phrased as in came the artist: IN CAME RA.
explanation.definitionFit: In camera is a legal phrase for proceedings held in private, away from the public and press.

clue.text: Mum with little hesitation leaving insect

indicators.note: something leaving goes away, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: mum is mother
er is a short pause in speech

explanation.surface: Mother quickly walks away from a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A moth is a winged nocturnal creature related to butterflies, drawn to lights.
